subject: POC success criteria & trial hosting options — Clearwell Health
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Chen <amy@clearwellhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC recap + next steps (success criteria & hosting options)

Hi Amy —

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have alignment before we draft a formal POC plan: 

Call recap
- Goals: validate end-to-end clinical note summarization and patient Q&A latency under 200ms for short queries, and embedding similarity recall > 0.86 on your benchmark set.
- Data: subset of de-identified clinical notes + 500 synthetic queries from your QA team.
- Risks: data residency and network egress; likely procurement timeline ~3–4 weeks.

Suggested success criteria (initial)
1) Latency: 95th percentile generation < 300ms for 128-token summaries (target < 200ms).
2) Accuracy: F1 >= 0.78 on internal labeled set for extraction pieces; embedding similarity mean >= 0.86.
3) Stability: no unhandled errors during 4-hour load test at 10rps.

Hosting options (pros/cons, rough timelines)
- Hosted API (fastest): Spin up in our hosted environment. Pros: 48–72h to demo, minimal ops. Cons: data flow via TLS to our region, not ideal for strict residency.
- Dedicated sandbox (reserved GPUs): Pros: predictable throughput, pin model. Timeline: ~2 weeks for capacity reservation & onboarding.
- VPC trial (preferred for PHI): Private control plane with customer VPC peering or dedicated private link. Timeline: ~3–4 weeks including networking, IAM, and KMS integration.

Immediate asks
- Please confirm which hosting option you prefer for the trial (hosted / dedicated sandbox / VPC).
- If VPC, please send the network and security contacts for kickoff and confirm the approximate procurement timeline.

I'll draft a short POC plan with owners and timeline once you confirm hosting choice. Attaching an internal quick MOP draft and a network whitelist template we typically use.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-poc-mop-v1.pdf]
[Attachment: network-whitelist-template.xlsx]

From: Amy Chen <amy@clearwellhealth.com>

Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2028 11:05:42 -0700
Subject: Re: POC recap + next steps (success criteria & hosting options)

Thanks Soojin — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The product team strongly prefers a VPC trial because of our PHI handling rules. Hosted API is okay only for a narrow eval of latency but not for sample PHI.
- On success criteria: can you add a throughput criterion — sustained 50 concurrent users with median latency under 250ms? Our internal test harness will simulate this.
- Procurement: procurement@clearwellhealth.com handles the SOW and has standard security addenda. Procurement lead is Karen Park (procurement@clearwellhealth.com).

We can commit to providing the 500 de-ID notes by next Tuesday (6/14). Can you provide a brief list of the network ports and IP ranges you will need so our network team can pre-approve?

Thanks — Amy
Amy Chen
Head of Product, Clearwell Health

Amy + team — great, thanks for the notes and for confirming VPC preference. I pulled together a concise POC plan below with timelines and owners. Please review and flag anything missing.

POC goal (two-week validation window)- Validate functional accuracy and production-like latency/throughput for clinical summarization and QA over a representative data slice.

Key success criteria (finalized)
- Latency: 95th < 300ms; median < 200ms for 128-token summaries.
- Throughput: sustain 50 concurrent users (approx 12 tokens/sec aggregate) with median latency < 250ms.
- Embedding recall: mean similarity >= 0.86 on your benchmark.
- Stability: zero critical service errors during a 4-hour soak at target throughput.

Hosting & timeline
- VPC trial (recommended): Kickoff week of 6/19. Activities: network allowlist, IAM role mapping, KMS integration (if required), and model onboarding. Target dry-run 6/26, validation window 6/27–7/10.
- Dedicated sandbox (fallback): If networking blocks, we can run a dedicated reserved pool. Timeline: ~2 weeks setup — target start 6/26.
- Hosted API (demo only): demo within 48–72h for latency checks against synthetic data.

Ownership (Redwood / Clearwell)
- Redwood: Soojin (sales eng) — POC coordinator; Ben Carter (infra eng) — VPC/network lead; Marissa Cole (CS) — success criteria & eval harness integration.
- Clearwell: Amy Chen — product sponsor; David Lin — network & infra contact; Karen Park / procurement@clearwellhealth.com — PO/SOW.

Attachments (for network team)
- network-whitelist-template.xlsx (IP ranges, ports, CIDR)
- redwood-poc-mop-v1.pdf (runbook + test plan)

Immediate asks
1) Confirm kickoff week 6/19 for VPC trial (Y/N).
2) Share network contact + best time to sync (David, cc'd above).
3) Procurement: if you can share your standard security addendum we can pre-run legal review in parallel.

If that looks good I'll convert into a short mutual action plan and share a calendar invite for a brief kickoff.

Best,
Soojin

Amy — adding a couple technical notes for your network/security team so they can validate against the whitelist template: 

- We support TLS 1.2+ and recommend TLS 1.3.
- For the VPC peering option we will need the following outbound ranges open: 34.210.16.0/22, 35.177.128.0/20 (these are the egress ranges used by the staging cluster).
- Ephemeral port ranges: 10240–65535 (for NAT/egress).
- If you require in-line inspection via an IDS, please note we also support IPSec VPN if peering isn't feasible.

I'll attach the whitelist template with the fields filled in for staging. Happy to hop on a short 20m call with your network engineer.

—Ben
Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: network-whitelist-template.xlsx]
